edits.english: Rav Asi says: And with regard to a ruling, to determine what constitutes the majority of a congregation, one should follow the majority of the residents of Eretz Yisrael alone, as they are the ones who determine this, as it is stated: “And Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath until the Brook of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days” (I Kings 8:65). And we will clarify what is stated in this verse: Since it is written: “And all Israel with him,” if so, why do I need to add: “A great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath until the Brook of Egypt”? What does this come to add? Conclude from it: The additional verse comes to teach us that these residents of Eretz Yisrael are called a congregation; but those others who are outside Eretz Yisrael are not called a congregation.
Rav Asi says: And with regard to a ruling - For we hold that if the court ruled erroneously and the majority of the congregation acted according to their ruling, they bring a bull.

Follow the majority of its residents in Eretz Yisrael - For those who are outside Eretz Yisrael are not included in the count, nor are those from the Brook of Egypt and beyond, as that is outside Eretz Yisrael.

Rav Asi says: And with regard to a ruling, to determine what constitutes the majority of a congregation, one should follow the majority of the children of Israel, only the residents of Eretz Yisrael are the ones who determine this, as it is stated: 'And Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath until the Brook of Egypt, before the Lord our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days' (I Kings 8:65). And we will clarify what is stated in this verse: Since it is written: 'And all Israel with him,' if so, why do I need 'a great congregation, from the entrance of Hamath until the Brook of Egypt'? What does this come to add? Conclude from it: The additional verse comes to teach us that these residents of Eretz Yisrael are called a congregation; but those others who are outside Eretz Yisrael are not called a congregation.
A great congregation from the entrance of Hamath - Even though we do not derive matters of Torah law from the words of the Prophets, this is merely a clarification of a matter.
